body: Adaline helps AI teams improve their agents autonomously, so you can find fires before they happen, ship fixes in minutes, and feel confidence in their agents — for the first time.
Adaline ingests production traces and groups recurring agent patterns into behavior maps your team can inspect.
Adaline generates evals from detected behaviors and user feedback, so regressions are caught before agent changes ship.

Synthesized 6 negative feedback samples mentioning 'spinning', 'never converges', 'doom loop' across 3 behaviors (plan-loops, long-refactor, ambiguous-refactor). The signal that distinguishes a productive replan from a doom-loop is step_overflow > budget * 1.3 combined with context_thrash > 2 — neither alone is sufficient because long but successful refactors also overflow step budgets.

Trajectory judge over LLM consensus (gpt-4 + claude-3.5) was chosen over a deterministic step-count assertion because step counts alone produce 18% false positives on long-but-converging plans where the agent eventually finds a clean diff. Recovery_rate is the load-bearing signal — it's what separates a 40-step success from a 40-step failure.
Coverage rose from 0.42 → 0.79 against the held-out set. Expected false-positive rate 4.2% on the 14d rolling window. Promotes to production after 48h stable — current run has been clean for 31h.
Adaline generates production-faithful synthetic data for the scenarios you keep meaning to cover and the ones you never knew existed.
Adaline is the ML layer between your traces and your agent diffs — behaviors, evals, data. Cursor and Claude are the “make no mistake” guesses; this is the feedback loop grounded in real signals.
“Adaline has become an invaluable tool for my team to develop GenAI products...”
Tan S.
